summary: Douglas County lookout on Dutchman Butte: a 1930s timber tower, then a 1970 steel tower from a radar site; NHLR-registered 2000; said to stand until winter 2026, with no current description found.

facts.design: 14x14 ft flat-top live-in cab on a three-legged steel tower erected in 1970; the earlier wooden lookout was about 10 to 12 ft tall
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts county list marks the site gone; firelookout.com says the structure remained on site until winter 2026 and does not say how it came down; no source describes the site today

staffing.status: staffed by the Douglas Forest Protective Association when registered in 2000; firelookout.com says staffed into the 2000s

events.note: Newspaper says a lookout station was constructed on Dutchman Butte as a shared post for the Douglas and Coos county patrols; the structure is not described
August 1, 1934 note from the Umpqua forest supervisor to the regional forester describes a 10-foot tower of Douglas fir logs on concrete blocks; conflicts with the 1936 date
CCC crew from Camp Bradford built a timber tower of about 10 feet with a 14x14 hip-roof cab (Forest Lookouts); NHLR and firelookout.com say a 12-ft wooden live-in tower was first here in 1936
Douglas FPA spent $179.18 to connect the lookout telephone line with the Forest Service line to West Fork
Radio number at this time was 518; telephone connections ran through Pacific Telephone to the Roseburg headquarters
Old lookout structure replaced by a 14'8" three-leg steel tower with a 14x14 flat-roof cab (Forest Lookouts); NHLR says a 15-ft guyed tower from the U.S. Air Force was erected in 1970
Survey station description (described by Douglas County, 1970): brass disk on the southeast foundation block of an old lookout tower
Registered March 1, 2000; nominated by Howard Verschoor, Oregon Registrar
NHLR says the lookout is staffed by the Douglas FPA; firelookout.com says staffed into the 2000s
Firelookout.com says the structure remained on site until the winter of 2026; the removal itself is not described

corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page gives the 1970 steel tower as 14 feet 8 inches (about 4.5 m) and the register gives 15 feet (about 4.6 m). No source read gives 3.0 m.

The 1970 steel tower replaced an earlier wooden lookout that had stood on the butte since the 1930s, per the Forest Lookouts page and firelookout.com. The register's Built field gives 1970, so this is a change of label, not of date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR gives 3,810 ft (1,161 m); firelookout.com gives 3907 ft. The brief keeps the NHLR figure of 1,161.3 m. The story does not give an elevation.

The sources give a 1925 station, a 10-foot tower in 1934, a CCC timber tower of about 10 feet in 1936 (Forest Lookouts), and a 12-foot wooden live-in tower in 1936 (NHLR and firelookout.com). The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one.

The Forest Fire Lookout Association county list says Gone, but firelookout.com says the structure remained on site until the winter of 2026. Both agree the tower is no longer standing. The sources do not give a removal date or cause, so the story uses firelookout's wording only.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 3.0 is not supported; corrected to 4.5 m (14'8"). The first-tower dates conflict (1925/1934/1936) and the register's 1936 height conflicts with the Forest Lookouts page. Only firelookout.com dates the structure to winter 2026; no source describes what, if anything, stands on the site now or whether it is accessible. Access fields left out for that reason. Second search found nothing new on the removal. Photos not added. Fact-check 2026-10-09: all dated claims checked against the Forest Lookouts, NHLR and firelookout.com pages (May 26, 1925; Aug 1, 1934; 1936; 1939; 1958; 1970; March 1, 2000); no factual errors found. Story wording changed only where it copied quote text closely.
